questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture and in which country it was in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very good, the begninning was very confusing because they are not used to accepting pharmacy students from Copenhagen University, so you got a lot of different information.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: A bit hard because you get a lot of information through many many mails, but in the end it's okay and you figure it out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You had a contact person, which other people from your country are assigned to, and this person is always available for you if you need any help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: USYD has different campus housing and if you apply within the deadline you are guaranteed a place to live. It's not always the cheapest option if you apply late.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In my building (Queen Mary Building) there was a big kitchen which everybody in the building used. It was a dirty kitchen sometimes, but was always available for you. No meal plans-

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: That it is first come first serve. So if you apply early there is a better chance for you to get the cheap housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It took some time, but it was straightforward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They need a lot of information as your transcript of records, photo of yourself, your intended units (not binding and you have about 1-2 weeks to change your mind). If your grades are a bit lower you need a  roof of English proficiency

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Yes, you could contact the uni if you had any questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look into if there are exams (not all courses have that) and look at the schedule (when they are released) as you are not allowed to have clashing classes.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The BA level of pharmacy classes were quite easy. A lot of the syllabus were things that we had already covered in the classes at UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Yeah, a mix of lecures, labs and classes were you solved tasks.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. Bachelor Thesis (Pharmacy Honours)
2. Outdoor Education
3. Drug Design and Development

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Outdoor Education. It is a class that a lot of exchange students do. It is chill and you meet a lot of cool people from around the world.

questions.answer: Visa, Non-refundable acceptance fee (accomondation) and student services and amenities fee.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Transport and food (was cheaper than my offical budget which I listed here).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A LOT of opportunities to do stuff outside uni.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Almost everything you can imagine. They had over 200 student clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Hiking, surfing, wakeboarding, food society and if you wanna learn about another culture then you can also join their society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go around and travel as much as you can. See as much of Australia as you can cause it is truly a beautiful country. Everything from Western Australia, Uluru, Tasmania, East Coast and much more.
Also a lot of things to do around Sydney (and many beaches)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Start talking to them from the first class. People here are very welcoming and are happy to include you.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: A lot of small talk and you have to get used to the dialect haha.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity from the Aboriginals to the Australians.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Bring sunscreen (UV here is dangerous).
Be open to meet people from other cultures.
Remember to take time for yourself to recharge.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sydney is an expensive city, escpecially things like alcohol cost a lot. But honestly a great experience, and the city is wonderful. You will quickly meet other students who shares your passions.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting so many people from so many different cultures. Really got a good friend group who showed me different perspectives.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That people will challenge your beliefs and your viewpoints. Sometimes it can feel annoying but just embace it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
